neighbours.label: soft, tender or defenceless as a bodily quality (soft, tender, helpless, legless), firing around the adjective; hard or strong counterparts in the same frames stay quiet
fire: Young caterpillars chew the tender shoots of the vine.
Unlike crabs, these worms have soft bodies with no shell.
Hatchlings are blind, soft and helpless for several days.
The chick's beak is still soft and easily damaged.
Slugs are soft creatures that dry out in the sun.
Beetle grubs are pale, legless and tender.
Newborn mice lie helpless in the nest for a week.
The fish has soft lips, so the hook tears out.
quiet: Old caterpillars chew the woody stems of the vine.
Like crabs, these animals have hard bodies with a shell.
Adults are alert, fast and strong within several days.
The eagle's beak is already hard and very sharp.
Beetles are armoured creatures that survive in the sun.
Stag beetles are dark, armoured and tough.
Adult mice run around the barn at night all week.
The fish has bony jaws, so the hook holds firm.
